content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Stripe alternatives

Each option offers a mix of tools and services that cater to specific needs, but they all share a common weakness: relying on a central authority to facilitate payments and manage orders. Gumroad, for instance, provides an easy-to-use interface for creators to sell digital products, but its reliance on PayPal and Stripe means that creators in restricted countries are locked out. Meanwhile, Lemon Squeezy and Paddle offer more comprehensive e-commerce solutions, but their infrastructure is still built on top of restricted payment gateways. Even PayPal, with its vast user base, is not immune to the problem of restricted countries, as Nigerian, Ghanaian, and Pakistani creators know all too well. The solution, therefore, lies not in patching up these platforms but in building infrastructure from the ground up, free from the constraints of restricted payment gateways.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

The platforms mentioned above handle restricted countries in different ways, but the outcome is always the same: creators in these countries are left high and dry. Stripe, for example, operates in only 46 countries out of 195, leaving many creators in restricted countries without access to its payment infrastructure. PayPal, on the other hand, can suspend an account at any time, holding funds for up to 180 days with no appeal. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy follow suit, relying on PayPal and Stripe to process payments. Even Paddle, with its more comprehensive e-commerce solution, can't escape the limitations of restricted payment gateways. The consequences of these restrictions are dire: creators in restricted countries are forced to rely on workarounds, abandon their digital projects, or even switch to offline business models. But there's a better way: infrastructure that puts creators in the driver's seat, free from platform dependencies and restrictions.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Payment speed, fees, and real costs are critical factors to consider when choosing a digital commerce infrastructure. While Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy offer relatively fast payment processing, their reliance on PayPal and Stripe means that creators in restricted countries are charged exorbitant fees. PayPal, with its vast user base, offers competitive fees, but its account suspension policy can leave creators high and dry. Paddle, with its more comprehensive e-commerce solution, charges higher fees but offers more features. The real cost, however, lies not in these fees but in the infrastructure itself – the reliance on central authorities to facilitate payments and manage orders. With a sovereign commerce infrastructure, creators can process payments in real-time, with no intermediaries to slow them down or charge them exorbitant fees.
